text: slide | "I. WIND DEPOSITION" | "Question 1" | ["The wall, the stone and the bush are obstacles. What happens to the speed of the wind when it meets an obstacle?"]
slide | "I. WIND DEPOSITION" | "Answer" | ["The wind slows down behind the obstacle. When it slows down, it loses its energy and drops the sand it carries. This is called wind deposition."]
slide | "I. WIND DEPOSITION" | "Question 2" | ["Apart from an obstacle, give another reason why the wind may drop the sand and dust it carries."]

slide | "I. WIND DEPOSITION" | "Answer" | ["The wind also drops its load when its speed falls in calm weather, or when it meets damp ground or rain, which makes the dust stick and fall."] | "Transition: In the desert, where there is a lot of sand, deposition builds dunes."
imageFull | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Activity 2: Study the diagram" | "A sand dune seen from the side." | "dune_profile.jpg"
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Question 1" | ["Which slope of the dune faces the wind? Is it gentle or steep?"]
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Answer" | ["The windward slope faces the wind. It is long and gentle. The other side, the leeward slope or slip face, is short and steep."]
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Question 2" | ["The wind pushes sand up the windward slope, and the sand falls down the slip face. What happens to the whole dune over time?"]
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Answer" | ["The dune moves slowly forward in the direction of the wind. This is why dunes can cover roads, fields and villages."]

imageQ | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Question 3" | "This dune is shaped like a crescent. In which direction do its horns point?" | "barchan_plan.png" | "Point to the wind arrows first, then to the horns."
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Answer" | ["The horns point downwind, in the direction the wind is blowing. This crescent-shaped dune is called a barchan."]
imageQ | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Question 4" | "These dunes are long, narrow and parallel. From how many directions does the wind blow?" | "seif.png"
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Answer" | ["The wind blows from two different directions. These long, narrow ridges of sand are called seif dunes."]
slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Question 5" | ["The Harmattan carries very fine dust far from the Sahara. What do we call a thick layer of this fine dust deposited by the wind?"]

slide | "II. DEPOSITIONAL FEATURES" | "Answer" | ["A thick layer of fine wind-blown dust is called loess. The largest area of loess is the Loess Plateau in China."] | "Transition: Now, copy the board summary."
sum | "I. Wind Deposition (1/2)" | "DEFINITION" | ["Wind deposition is the dropping of sand and dust by the wind when it loses its energy."]

sum | "I. Wind Deposition (2/2)" | ["The wind deposits its load for the following reasons:","– The speed of the wind decreases.","– The wind meets an obstacle, such as a rock, a bush or a wall.","– The wind meets damp ground or rain."]
sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (1/8)" | ["The main features formed by wind deposition are sand dunes and loess. The two main types of sand dunes are barchans and seif dunes."]
sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (2/8)" | "A. Sand Dunes" | ["A sand dune is a hill or a ridge of sand piled up by the wind."]

sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (3/8)" | "A. Sand Dunes" | ["The various characteristics of a sand dune are:","– The windward slope faces the wind and is gentle.","– The leeward slope, or slip face, is steep.","– The dune moves slowly in the direction of the wind."]
sumImage | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (4/8)" | "B. Barchans" | "A barchan is a crescent-shaped dune whose horns point downwind." | "barchan_plan.png"
sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (5/8)" | "B. Barchans" | ["A barchan forms where the wind blows steadily from one direction and where there is not much sand."]
sumImage | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (6/8)" | "C. Seif Dunes" | "A seif dune is a long, narrow ridge of sand, parallel to other seifs." | "seif.png"
sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (7/8)" | "C. Seif Dunes" | ["Seif dunes form where the wind blows from two different directions. They can be many kilometres long."]

sum | "II. Depositional Features of Wind Action (8/8)" | "D. Loess" | ["Loess is a thick layer of fine, yellowish dust deposited by the wind far from the desert. The largest area of loess is the Loess Plateau in China."]

d.coverNote: Good morning, class. In Lesson 27 we saw how the wind erodes. Today, in Lesson 28, we see what the wind builds when it drops its sand.

d.lesson: Lesson 28: Depositional Features of Wind Action
d.focus: Depositional features of wind action; sand dunes (barchans and seif dunes).
d.competence: Learners are able to explain why sand and dust pile up behind walls, stones and bushes, and to recognise barchan and seif dunes.
objectives: Explain why the wind deposits the sand and dust it carries.
Describe the structure and movement of a sand dune.
Distinguish between barchan and seif dunes, and define loess.
recall: Wind erodes the land by deflation, abrasion and attrition.
Wind erosion forms rock pedestals, zeugen, yardangs and inselbergs.
The sand and dust removed by the wind must be dropped somewhere.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: where did learners find piles of sand in their compound?
situation: After a windy Harmattan day, Aminatou sweeps her family compound in Garoua. She sees that the sand has piled up only in some places: at the foot of a wall, behind a big stone and around a bush.
In the open parts of the compound, there is almost no sand. Aminatou does not understand why the wind drops its sand in some places and not in others.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Aminatou does not understand why the wind drops its sand in some places and not in others.
In which places did the sand pile up in Aminatou's compound?
The sand piled up at the foot of a wall, behind a big stone and around a bush.
What can Aminatou's family do to stop sand from piling up near the house?
They can plant a hedge or put up a fence some distance from the house, so that the wind drops its sand there.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand where and why the wind drops its sand, and to recognise the dunes it builds in the desert.

evaluation: On which side of a dune do we find the slip face?
The slip face is on the leeward side, the side sheltered from the wind.
Give one difference between a barchan and a seif dune.
A barchan is crescent-shaped and forms with wind from one direction. A seif dune is a long, straight ridge and forms with winds from two directions.
Why can moving dunes be a danger for people living near the desert?
Moving dunes can bury roads, fields, wells and houses.
remediation: The dropping of sand by the wind is called wind ______.
The side of a dune that faces the wind is the ______ slope.
The steep side of a dune is called the slip ______.
A crescent-shaped dune is called a ______.
Long, parallel dunes formed by winds from two directions are called ______ dunes.
A thick layer of fine wind-blown dust is called ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. deposition 2. windward 3. face 4. barchan 5. seif 6. loess
end.homework: Ask an elder in your family how people in your area cope with the heat, the dust and the shortage of water during the dry season. Write down two ways.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 29: Man in the Hot Desert Environments.
end.matter: I. Wind deposition (definition and causes); II. Depositional features: sand dunes (structure and movement), barchans, seif dunes, loess.
teacherNote: If possible, bring a tray of dry sand and a small stone, and blow gently across it to show how sand collects behind an obstacle.
Remind learners that the horns of a barchan always point downwind: this is a frequent exam mistake.
The Harmattan dust in Garoua comes largely from the Sahara, especially the Bodélé Depression in Chad.
